name: The Disc
description: A man from Ashwick spent his life on the mark in Brennan's margins, worked out how to wake the grey key that bears it, and went east with it. He did not come back. Find out how far he got.

steps.description: Brennan knows of a man who kept a cottage in Ashwick, studied how to wake the key, then went east and never came back. His work should still be in the house he left.
steps.hint: Maren's Cottage is south of the East Edge of Ashwick, a long road north of Greenford. If it is dark, type cast glow first. In the cottage, type search.

steps.description: His journal gives the method for waking the disc with light at a hearth cut to the mark. It never answered here. He took the disc and followed a surveyor's marks east, to cut another hearth where the thing could be seen.
steps.hint: Reth's trail leaves the North Vale Road in Kingsbarrow, east through a hedge-gap it takes a search to find. Ask the one who came back, at the shelter past the Wind-Gap.

steps.description: The one who came back saw him: a thin man with a mattock on his back and something grey he kept in his fist, walking toward the split stone.
steps.hint: Reth's route names a cairn split by lightning. Search there for any sign of him. Bring a light after dark.

steps.description: On a fallen stone of the cairn, cut fresh once and weathered since: a ring struck through with a line, and an arrow east, to the old survey camp.
steps.hint: He went on to the old survey camp Reth spoke of. Search it. Bring a light after dark.

steps.description: He slept at the survey camp and went on with his tools, east, past where the green stops. Something up there has claimed that ground since.
steps.hint: The Reach-Alpha holds the line where the green fails. His trail goes on past it. Bring friends, and kill it.

steps.description: The alpha is dead, and the way past the green is open. Someone cleared earth off the buried face by hand, not far from here.
steps.hint: Follow the buried face to where it was cleared by hand. Search the camp you find there. Bring a light after dark.

steps.description: You found him under the fallen lean-to, and in his satchel the grey disc. Beside him lies a hearthstone cut to the mark, the last thing he made. He never finished.
steps.hint: His method wakes the disc with light at a hearth cut to the mark. His own is here. Type cast glow.

steps.description: The disc woke at his hearthstone, and it keeps the light now. It has also roused something. The Sentinel at the buried face turns toward it.
steps.hint: The Sentinel stands near the door, and the Keeper will open nothing while it does. Nothing you can do alone will move it. Bring friends.

steps.description: The Sentinel is down, and the door is close. The one who keeps its threshold has watched this road for a long time.
steps.hint: The Keeper sits at the Disc-Door. Bring her the woken disc. Type talk keeper.

steps.description: You carry the woken disc, the last of a lost man's work, done at last by a stranger's hand. The door answers it.

rewards.actor: The Keeper looks at the disc, then at the road behind you, as if counting someone who is not there. "He sat here once, you know. One night, on his way up. He would not say his name, and I did not ask him for it." She turns back to her fire. The door waits.
rewards.observer: The Keeper looks long at the grey disc in {actor}'s hand.

actions.actor: You work the loose stone free of its neighbors. It grinds aside and shows a small cavity in the wall behind it. Inside, a folded letter lies against the back of the hollow, hidden there on purpose.
You ease the folded page out from under the table leg, and the table rocks.
You lift the newer sheets and unpin the torn page from beneath them.
You work the folded page out from under the bar. The salt has made it stiff.
You peel the page off the bench. The ink has run, but it holds together.
You draw the torn page from between the volumes. One side of it is burned.
You slide the torn page out of the gap in the registers. No one has written it down.
You reach under the last desk and bring out a torn leaf, older than anything being copied here.
In the last pew a hymnal falls open at a torn page that is no part of it. You take it.

You sit at the cold table and read the man's life backward.
Years of it: a hand that starts careful and turns driven, the
same questions put a hundred ways to one buried thing far to
the east. Something made, he is certain, and old past any
reckoning, and wrong in a way he never quite sets down in
words. He calls it only the thing. The ring struck through with
a line is inked in every margin, worried at like a sore tooth.
Then the method, worked out slow across many pages, for waking
the grey disc that is its key: light, held over it at a hearth
cut to the mark. He cut this one himself. It never answered, and
near the end he stops asking why. The thing is too far off, he
writes. He will take the disc east, along the surveyor's marks,
and cut another where it can be seen. The last line is not about
the thing at all. It is a name, set down once and gently, as if
to keep one soft thing safe. Maren. He went east to finish this.
He did not come back to her.

actions.observer: {actor} reads a long while at the cottage table.

actions.actor: Among the stones the lightning threw down, one has been turned to face the road. Cut into it, fresh once and weathered since, is a ring struck through with a line, and beside it a short, hard arrow: east, toward the old camp Reth spoke of. Not Reth's hand. His cuts are neater than this.

actions.observer: {actor} turns over the fallen stones of the cairn.

actions.actor: Under the bleached poles someone has slept more recently than the surveyors. A flint tin, empty. A boot-print of old ash at the fire ring. On the pole nearest the fire the same mark is cut, and under it, smaller, a tally of days that stops at nine. Whoever he was, he left his bedding and took his tools, east, past where the green stops. There are tracks over his now, large ones, and they do not care who has walked here.

actions.observer: {actor} searches the ruins of the old camp.

actions.actor: The alpha is down, and the ground it held lies open to the east, bare and wrong and very quiet.
The lining of the satchel is empty now. You already hold his spare. Type cast glow to wake it.
In the lining of the satchel your fingers find a second grey disc, cool and dead in the hand, the twin of the one you woke. He had brought a spare. Of course he had.

Under the fallen lean-to, where a man would lie who meant to get up in
the morning, there is a strap, a coat gone to threads and not many bones.
He is lying on his side, facing the grey. Against his ribs is a satchel,
and in the satchel a flint tin, a book you do not open, and a disc of pale
grey metal, cool and heavier than its size. By his hand lies a hearthstone
carried a very long way, cut with the same mark, and cut again, and cut
again. The chisel is still beside it. He was almost done. It wants only
what he did not have left to give it: light, held over it, patiently. Type
cast glow.

actions.observer: {actor} kneels a long time under the fallen lean-to.

actions.actor: You set the grey disc into the cut of his hearthstone and hold the glow over it, as his method says. The lines warm, and the mark at the center wakes.
The disc is still in his satchel. You take it.

You set the disc into the cut of his hearthstone, where the marks draw
inward to a single point, and you hold the soft glow over it, patient
and exact, the way a driven man worked out alone and wrote down so a
stranger might one day do this right. For a long moment, nothing. Then
the grey face warms under your fingers, not with your warmth but its own.
The fine raised lines drink the light and keep it, holding a glow a
half-breath past when it should fade, and the ring-struck mark at the
center wakes and steadies, sure of where it belongs. His work, done at
last, a few paces from where he lay down. And along the buried face, not
far off, something very large and very patient turns to look at you.

actions.observer: {actor} holds a soft glow over a cut stone, and the air goes briefly strange.

actions.actor: The Sentinel stops, all at once, the way a thing stops when it has only ever been waiting. The disc warms against your side. The door is close.
